gloss: how something looks in a photo; quality of a photograph

definitions.gloss: how something appears in a photograph; photographic quality
definitions.explanation: The way a subject looks when captured in a photograph. Refers to whether someone or something looks good or bad in pictures.

examples.japanese: この{写真|しゃしん}は{写|うつ}りがいい。
{彼女|かのじょ}は{写|うつ}りが{悪|わる}いだけで、{実物|じつぶつ}はもっときれいだ。
examples.english: She just doesn't photograph well — she looks much prettier in person.

examples.japanese: このカメラはレンズがいいから、{写|うつ}りが{全然|ぜんぜん}{違|ちが}う。
examples.english: This camera has a good lens, so the photo quality is completely different.

notes:
Derived from the verb {写|うつ}る (to be photographed). Commonly used to discuss how flattering or unflattering photos are. Very common in everyday conversation about photography and selfies.

FORMS:
Noun form of {写|うつ}る (to be photographed, to appear in a photo).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {写|うつ}りがいい: to look good in photos; to photograph well
- {写|うつ}りが{悪|わる}い: to look bad in photos; not photogenic
- {写|うつ}りを{気|き}にする: to worry about how one looks in photos

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {映|うつ}り: how something looks on screen (TV, video) — different kanji for video/screen contexts
- {写真|しゃしん}{写|うつ}り: specifically how one looks in photographs

USAGE:
The expression {写|うつ}りがいい/わるい is one of the most common ways to talk about being photogenic or not in Japanese.
